note: Explanatory slides for the journal club. Figures marked 'schematic' are illustrations, not data from the paper.

slides.title: Instantons: tunnelling between QCD vacua
text: The QCD vacuum has infinitely many degenerate classical minima, labelled by the Chern–Simons number $N_{CS}$. Instantons are Euclidean solutions that tunnel between neighbouring minima, changing the topological charge $Q$.
math: Q=\frac{g^2}{32\pi^2}\int d^4x\; G^a_{\mu\nu}\tilde G^{a\,\mu\nu}=\Delta N_{CS}\in\mathbb Z

figure.caption: Periodic vacuum structure: the system oscillates in one vacuum, then tunnels under the barrier to the next ($\Delta N_{CS}=1$).

slides.title: Chirality violation: the ’t Hooft vertex
text: Through the axial anomaly, an instanton changes the chirality of every light quark flavour at once.
bullets: One quark–antiquark pair of each light flavour, plus gluons, produced together
Predicted rates are large at low instanton mass but carry large theoretical uncertainties

figure.caption: Instanton-induced process: two incoming gluons, a multi-particle final state with all light flavours.

slides.title: The signature: isotropy
text: Ordinary QCD events are collimated and back-to-back. An instanton decays ‘democratically’ into many soft particles, spherically in its rest frame. Event-shape variables capture the difference.

figure.caption: Transverse view: collimated QCD activity (left) versus an isotropic instanton-like event (right).

slides.title: The ATLAS search
bullets: 1.6 nb⁻¹ of 13 TeV pp collisions at very low instantaneous luminosity (almost no pile-up)
Reconstructed charged tracks → angular variables → classifier
Minimum-bias background predicted with a data-driven technique and reweighted Monte Carlo
Profile-likelihood fit in a two-dimensional classifier variable

figure.caption: Analysis chain, from tracks to the fit.

slides.title: Result: a 3.5σ excess
text: The fit finds more low-mass isotropic events than the background model predicts.
bullets: Observed significance 3.5σ: suggestive, not a discovery
Needs confirmation and scrutiny of the background modelling

figure.caption: How an excess on top of a falling background looks in a classifier-score distribution.

slides.title: For the discussion
bullets: Is minimum bias modelled well enough at low multiplicity and low mass?
Cross-checks: strangeness content, other experiments, other energies
Theory: instanton size distribution and normalisation of the rate
